correction_1_what_7_4_G_actually_is.and_the_order_s_own_characterisation_is_: the order states the 7.4 GiB figure is a resident set and not a cgroup peak. Measured against the retained journal, the opposite is true of THAT number: it is systemd's cgroup peak for the scope. The order's substantive point stands and is stated below without relying on that premise.

the_number_that_IS_a_resident_set.provenance: MEMORY_GATE.jsonl measured_pilot_peak_bytes, taken from resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss inside one cell child (tools/df_e1_block.py:run_cell), i.e. ONE PROCESS'S RESIDENT SET

correction_1_what_7_4_G_actually_is.what_it_is: systemd's own end-of-unit line for the memory-gated wrapper scope: 'crispdm-q2deep-<epoch>-<pid>.scope: Consumed 21min 32.106s CPU time over 23min 9.019s wall clock time, 7.4G memory peak.'  It is therefore a CGROUP peak, not a resident set -- but of the WRAPPER SCOPE that hosted the pilot driver and its parallel children, taken AT AN oomd KILL, so it is a kill-time watermark of a multi-child tree and not any single cell's footprint.

master.note: tools/df_e1_block.py does not exist on master at all: the household block runner has never been merged there, so the two false flags above mean 'no such file', not 'no such code'

and_the_repair_is_stranded_on_one_branch.reading: the instrument exists on exactly one branch and on no other. The household block runner is not on master at all, and every feature branch any lane is working from carries the bare-subprocess launch and records only peak_rss_bytes -- so a successor cut from any of them would reproduce the same unusable figure.
and_the_repair_is_stranded_on_one_branch.repair_commit: 84bcd605 -- run_cell gained cost.cgroup_memory_peak_bytes and labelled the RSS figure with its basis
and_the_repair_is_stranded_on_one_branch.second_limitation_of_the_repair_itself: even on that branch the child still takes no scope, and LIMITS['parallel_children'] is 3, so cgroup_memory_peak_bytes read from a cell child returns the peak of the SHARED driver scope charging up to three concurrent cells. It is a per-batch figure, not a per-cell one.

correction_2_no_per_cell_cgroup_peak_exi.consequence: no cell-scoped memory.peak was ever created, so no successor cap may be declared from any Q2 cell's retained numbers
correction_2_no_per_cell_cgroup_peak_exi.mechanism: tools/df_e1_block.py:run_units launches every unit with a bare subprocess.run([sys.executable, ..., 'child', ...]).  It never invokes the launcher, so a cell child takes no scope of its own and inherits whatever cgroup the driver sits in.

what_was_measured_today_instead.why_it_survives_a_failure: memory.peak is a KERNEL HIGH-WATERMARK read from inside the child, not a sample and not a value the launcher writes back on release. It is therefore a measurement even for a child shorter than the sampler's interval, where a SAMPLED tree peak is only a floor, and it is not lost when a release never succeeds.
